title: redStackPRO topology
description: Provider-agnostic topology document. No provider vocabulary appears at this layer. Derived overlay fields and per-kind requirements live in the node kind registry, not in this document. Version 0.7.0 covers offense and defense modes.

schema_version.title: Schema version
schema_version.description: Pinned. One schema file per version. Migrations move documents between versions.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: The canvas mode: offense (attack infrastructure) or defense (an AD range to attack). Gates the palette, prefix, and chrome, not the compiler. Fixed at creation. Renamed from artie/haven in 0.7.0.

name.title: Topology name
name.description: Shown in the picker. It becomes the download file name and the guide title.

prefix.title: Name prefix
prefix.description: 1 to 8 lowercase letters or digits, starting with a letter. Prepended to every host's name, e.g. off plus myth-ts01 gives off-myth-ts01. Empty uses off on the offense canvas and def on the defense canvas. Prefix plus each host id must fit in 15 characters, so 3 to 4 letters is best (off, acme). Give each range you run at the same time its own prefix so their host names stay apart.

description.title: Description
description.description: Free text about this topology. Not deployed.

region.title: Region
region.description: Cloud region the deploy targets, e.g. us-east4 on GCP or us-east-1 on AWS. It becomes the region default in deploy.tfvars. Proxmox and ESXi ignore it.

domains.title: Your domains
domains.description: Domains you own, used to suggest redirector host names. Not deployed.

base_cidr.title: Address root
base_cidr.description: The block networks and subnets are carved from, default 10.0.0.0/8. Set it when the deploy has to sit inside a block you were given.

auto_stop.title: Auto-stop
auto_stop.description: Stops every instance of the range on a schedule so a forgotten range does not bill all night. Instances are stopped, not deleted: the range comes back as it was when you start it again with manage.sh start. Disks and reserved addresses keep billing. Off unless enabled. Runs on GCP, AWS and Azure; Proxmox and ESXi ignore it.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Turn the schedule on. Nothing is scheduled when off.

at.title: Stop at
at.description: Daily stop time, 24 hour HH:MM, e.g. 20:00.

after_hours.title: Stop after (hours)
after_hours.description: Stop this many hours after the first apply, then daily at that time. 1 to 168. Use it for a range started at an odd hour. When both this and Stop at are set, the earlier one wins.

timezone.title: Timezone
timezone.description: IANA zone the stop time is read in, e.g. Europe/London. Default UTC. Azure accepts only the common zones; an unknown one fails the Azure export.

provider.title: Deploy target
provider.description: The provider this topology was last set to download for. Canvas state: the download still targets whatever you pick at export.

blueprint.title: Source blueprint
blueprint.description: The shipped blueprint this topology started from, e.g. goad-light. Set by the canvas, which uses it to offer the matching extensions. Not deployed.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit, e.g. myth-ts01.

cidr.title: Address range
cidr.description: An IPv4 range in CIDR form, e.g. 10.30.0.0/16.

port.title: Port
port.description: A TCP or UDP port, 1 to 65535.

public_address.title: Public address
public_address.description: Give this host a public IP. Only possible in a subnet whose exposure is internet. Default: on for a jumpbox and a redirector, off for everything else.

position.title: Position
position.description: Canvas layout only. The compiler ignores this.

id.title: Id
id.description: The node's name, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. On the offense canvas it is a purpose slug, the kind tag and a two digit ordinal, e.g. myth-ts01, and the host name is the prefix plus this id. On the defense canvas the id is the host name.

width.title: Width
width.description: Canvas size for a container. Layout only; the compiler ignores it.

height.title: Height
height.description: Canvas size for a container. Layout only; the compiler ignores it.

pinned.title: Pinned id
pinned.description: You renamed this node by hand, so the canvas keeps the name instead of deriving one. Canvas state only.

overlay_siem.description: A defensive telemetry server on a range: a Wazuh or ELK box that collects from agents on the range hosts. Not domain joined; it sits on the subnet. See the GOAD wazuh and elk extensions.

product.title: SIEM product
product.description: wazuh installs a Wazuh manager, elk an Elasticsearch, Logstash and Kibana stack. Every Windows host in the range gets the matching agent.

os.title: Operating system
os.description: Linux image for this box. Empty uses Debian 13.

hostname.title: Host name
hostname.description: Computer name, 15 characters max: letters, digits and hyphens, e.g. wazuh.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: For you only; nothing reads it during the deploy.

internal_ip.title: Internal IP
internal_ip.description: A fixed private address inside this host's subnet, e.g. 192.168.56.50. Empty lets the provider pick one.

overlay_network.description: A routing domain. Members reach each other privately. Compiles to a VPC, a VNet, or a Proxmox bridge domain.

cidr.title: Address range
cidr.description: Address range for this network, e.g. 10.30.0.0/16. Filled in for you; change it only to fit a block you must use. Peered networks must not overlap.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Pins this network to one provider. Leave it empty: every network compiles to the deploy target you pick at download.

overlay_segment.description: A subnet inside exactly one network.

cidr.title: Address range
cidr.description: Address range for this subnet, e.g. 10.30.10.0/24, inside its network's range.

egress.title: Egress
egress.description: allowed: hosts can reach the internet (needed to install packages). none: no outbound access.

exposure.title: Exposure
exposure.description: Inbound reach, and the ceiling for the hosts in it. internet: a host here may take a public address. local: reachable only from inside the deployment. none: isolated. Each host still decides with its own public address setting, so a jumpbox and the boxes behind it can share a subnet.

tier.title: Tier
tier.description: A label for the canvas layout. Not deployed.

server.title: Web server
server.description: The reverse proxy that fronts the C2: apache or nginx.

hostname.title: Domain (FQDN)
hostname.description: Public name this redirector answers on, e.g. cdn.example.net. Required: you register it and point its A record at this redirector, so nothing can invent one for you.

cert_source.title: Certificate source
cert_source.description: letsencrypt (default): a real certificate once your DNS A record points here. self_signed: no public certificate; beacons must skip validation.

gating.title: Gating
gating.description: What separates a beacon from a scanner. A request missing the header or the prefix gets the decoy page, never the teamserver.

header_name.title: Header name
header_name.description: Header name your beacon sends: letters, digits, hyphens, e.g. X-Request-Id.

header_value.title: Header value
header_value.x-redstackpro-placeholder: leave blank for a random value
header_value.description: The value the header must carry. Leave it blank and a fresh random value is made at export, which is what you want: a value written in a blueprint is one everyone already knows. The C2 profile gets the same value.

redirect_rules.title: Block scanners
redirect_rules.description: Turn away known scanners, AV vendors and TOR exit nodes. Turn it off for lab work where that noise is the point.

decoy.title: Cover page
decoy.description: What a request without the header gets instead of the C2: a believable but fictional site for the named vertical. Default cdn.

decoy_asset_pack.title: Cover asset folder
decoy_asset_pack.description: Folder on the redirector holding your own cover images, named per slot (hero.jpg, intro.jpg, service-0.jpg, face-0.jpg, video.mp4). Copy the files to this path on the redirector after the first deploy, then run deploy.sh again to rebuild the cover page. Slots you leave out, or an empty value, use fetched stock imagery.

decoy_video.title: Cover video
decoy_video.description: Loop a video behind the cover page headline. Only an asset folder can supply one (video.mp4 or video.webm); without it the hero stays a still. Adds the clip's full weight to the page.

c2.title: C2 framework
c2.description: C2 framework installed on this box. none gives a plain Debian host for your own C2.

version.title: Version
version.description: Git tag or branch to install, e.g. v3.3.1. Empty installs the latest. Mythic and Adaptix only; Sliver always installs the current release.

sink.title: Log store
sink.description: Where shipped logs are stored and searched.

shipper.title: Shipper
shipper.description: The agent senders run. filebeat is the only one.

tls.title: TLS
tls.description: Encrypt log shipping with the jumpbox CA. Leave on.

services.title: Services
services.description: What the jumpbox runs. ssh is the management path; guacamole is the browser portal every guide uses. wireguard and openvpn here are ignored: the VPN follows access_mode.

certificate_authority.title: Certificate authority
certificate_authority.description: Builds the certificate authority that signs log shipping, Windows WinRM and OpenVPN certificates. Required while a collector uses TLS, a Windows operator exists, or access_mode is openvpn.

internal_ip.title: Internal IP
internal_ip.description: A fixed private address inside this host's subnet. Empty lets the provider pick one.

offensive_toolkit.title: Offensive toolkit
offensive_toolkit.description: Installs the foothold tools (impacket, certipy, coercer, netexec, bloodhound-python, hashcat). On by default on a defense range, off on an offense bastion, where the tools live on the operator box. Opens no ports.

access_mode.title: Access mode
access_mode.description: How operators reach this box. public: the portal on the jumpbox's public address. wireguard or openvpn: each operator gets a personal VPN credential, made at apply. Offense only; a defense range ignores it.

vpn_port.title: VPN port
vpn_port.description: The VPN listen port. Default 51820 for wireguard and 1194 for openvpn; set another, e.g. 443, to get through a restrictive network.

vpn_protocol.title: VPN protocol
vpn_protocol.description: Transport for the VPN. wireguard is udp only; openvpn takes udp or tcp, trading speed for reach through networks that block udp.

operators.title: Operators
operators.description: The people on this range, one entry each. Each gets a portal account and, with a VPN access mode, a VPN credential, made at apply. Empty leaves the single shared admin account. These are people, not operator boxes.

handle.title: Handle
handle.description: Login name, unique on this range: lowercase letters, digits, dot, underscore or hyphen, starting with a letter or digit, 32 characters max.

role.title: Role
role.description: A label such as lead, for display only. One line, no pipe character, 64 characters max.

os.title: Operating system
os.description: OS of this operator box. kali and debian are Linux; windows gives a Windows desktop over RDP.

desktop.title: Desktop
desktop.description: Linux only: installs a desktop and xrdp so this box opens as an RDP tile in the portal, for driving a web UI C2 without a Windows operator.

fqdn.title: Domain name (FQDN)
fqdn.description: Fully qualified domain name: at least two labels of letters, digits and hyphens, e.g. sevenkingdoms.local.

netbios.title: NetBIOS name
netbios.description: Short domain name, 1 to 15 letters or digits, e.g. SEVENKINGDOMS. Empty uses the first label of the FQDN, uppercased.

users.title: Users
users.description: The domain's user accounts. A user can hold a privilege and flaws that seed an attack path. The canvas can generate a realistic set.

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: Group memberships, e.g. Domain Admins, IT.

privilege.title: Privilege
privilege.description: user: an ordinary member. local_admin: added to local Administrators on every Windows member server (srv) in this domain. domain_admin and enterprise_admin: the escalation targets.

flaws.title: Flaws
flaws.description: Account misconfigurations that seed an attack path, e.g. kerberoastable (an SPN is set) or asrep_roastable (preauth disabled).

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Whether the account is enabled. Empty means enabled.

assumed_breach.title: Assumed breach
assumed_breach.description: The low-privilege user an operator starts as. Gets a portal tile on one workstation in this domain and is named in the briefing.

description.title: Description
description.description: The AD description field. The password_in_description flaw plants a password here.

spns.title: SPNs
spns.description: Service principal names on the account, e.g. HTTP/web.sevenkingdoms.local.

delegate_to.title: Delegate to
delegate_to.description: Services this account may delegate to (msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo), for the constrained_delegation flaw, e.g. CIFS/winterfell.north.sevenkingdoms.local.

weak_password.title: Weak password
weak_password.description: The weak password to set with the weak_password flaw. Empty uses a default.

password.title: Password
password.description: This account's own password, to reproduce a lab's real credentials. Empty uses the shared lab password.

ou.title: OU
ou.description: The OU at the domain root the user goes in. Empty uses the Users container.

planted_by.title: Planted by
planted_by.description: Canvas marker for a user added by ticking an account technique on a host. Not deployed.

acls.title: Access rights
acls.description: Dangerous rights one principal holds over another object, the edges an attack path walks, e.g. tywin.lannister has GenericAll over jaime.lannister.

principal.title: Principal
principal.description: Who holds the right: a user, a group or a computer (name$) on this domain, or DOMAIN\name for one in another domain.

target.title: Target
target.description: What the right is over: a user, a group, a computer (name$), an OU, or a distinguished name such as OU=Crownlands,DC=sevenkingdoms,DC=local.

right.title: Right
right.description: GenericAll, GenericWrite, WriteDacl, WriteOwner, WriteProperty, ReadProperty, GenericExecute, Self, ForceChangePassword, AddMember, or the extended rights Ext-User-Force-Change-Password, Ext-Write-Self-Membership, Ext-Self-Self-Membership and Ext-Write-SPN.

gmsa.title: gMSA accounts
gmsa.description: Group managed service accounts whose password the listed computers can read.

dns.title: DNS name
dns.description: Its DNS host name, e.g. gmsaDragon.essos.local.

spns.title: SPNs
spns.description: Service principal names on the account.

hosts.title: Readers
hosts.description: Computer names allowed to read the managed password.

laps_readers.title: LAPS readers
laps_readers.description: Users or groups allowed to read the LAPS local admin password.

group_members.title: Group nesting
group_members.description: Groups placed inside other groups: each parent group lists its member groups, e.g. Domain Admins: QueenProtector.

ous.title: OUs
ous.description: Organizational units created at the domain root, e.g. Crownlands.

groups.title: Extra groups
groups.description: Groups to create even though no user is in them, e.g. a group only an access right names. Groups named by users or by nesting are created anyway.

overlay_range_host.description: Shared settings for the range host kinds (dc, srv, wks, fw, appliance).

os.title: Operating system
os.description: Image this host boots. Empty builds Windows Server 2022 for a dc or srv and Windows 11 for a wks (fw and appliance are drawn but not built in this release). GCP and AWS have no Windows client image, so windows_10 and windows_11 boot Windows Server 2022 there. Windows 10 is past end of support. linux is a generic Debian 13 box.

hostname.title: Host name
hostname.description: Windows computer name, 15 characters max. Keep it equal to the id.

services.title: Services
services.description: Software to install on a Windows member server (srv): mssql (SQL Server), iis (IIS) or exchange. Use role for adcs and mecm. Any other value installs nothing.

role.title: Role
role.description: sql: installs SQL Server. adcs: an Enterprise CA (dc or srv). mecm: a MECM site (srv). web: badge only; add iis under services to install IIS. fileshare: badge only; add the Open share vuln for a share. generic: nothing.

edr.title: EDR label
edr.description: Label shown in the briefing only. To run Defender, tick Defender on. SIEM agents install automatically when the range has a Wazuh or ELK box.

defender_enabled.title: Defender on
defender_enabled.description: Keep Windows Defender real-time protection on for this host. Off by default. Windows hosts only.

endpoint_telemetry.title: Endpoint telemetry
endpoint_telemetry.description: Installs Sysmon and turns on command-line and directory-service auditing, so a SIEM sees the events detections need. Off by default. Windows hosts only.

vulns.title: Vulnerabilities
vulns.description: Attack-path misconfigurations and CVEs planted on this host, from the GOAD-derived catalog.

hardening.title: Hardening
hardening.description: Not applied yet: these controls are recorded but not deployed.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: For you only; nothing reads it during the deploy.

internal_ip.title: Internal IP
internal_ip.description: A fixed private address inside this host's subnet, e.g. 192.168.56.10. Empty lets the provider pick one. Set it when the deploy needs a predictable address.

vulns_vars.title: Vulnerability settings
vulns_vars.description: Settings the ticked vulnerabilities read, as one JSON object, e.g. a share path or a delegation target.

sudo_groups.title: Sudo groups
sudo_groups.description: Linux member server only: domain groups granted sudo, e.g. LinuxAdmins.

ssh_groups.title: SSH groups
ssh_groups.description: Linux member server only: domain groups allowed to SSH in. Empty allows all.

edge_attached.description: Membership. Host to segment, or segment to network. A segment attaches to exactly one network.

primary.title: Primary
primary.description: For a host in more than one subnet: exactly one attachment is primary.

edge_fronts.description: Redirector to teamserver. The source receives the target address. Many sources to one target is the rollover pool, which the compiler emits as a Terraform output for the operator to work into a C2 profile.

protocol.title: Protocol
protocol.description: The redirector serves https. Other values are not served yet.

listen_port.title: Listen port
listen_port.description: Port the redirector serves on. Only 443 is served; the beacon calls this port.

upstream_port.title: Upstream port
upstream_port.description: Port the redirector proxies to on the teamserver. Only 443 reaches the C2.

uri_prefix.title: URI prefix
uri_prefix.description: Path the redirector routes to this teamserver, e.g. /cdn/assets: lowercase letters, digits, slash, underscore and hyphen, starting with a slash. Two fronts edges from one redirector need different prefixes.

edge_logs_to.description: Sender to collector. The source receives the target address. Port and TLS come from the collector overlay so they cannot diverge per sender. The collector ingress rule is derived from the set of these edges, not from a segment range.

edge_manages.description: Jumpbox to network or segment. Members of the target receive the source address as a ProxyJump in the generated inventory. A host is excluded from its own proxy path.

edge_peers.description: Network to network. The two networks are peered so hosts in one can reach hosts in the other on private addresses, which is what lets a jumpbox or a collector serve across a routing domain boundary. Same cloud only, and the two networks must not have overlapping CIDRs. Bidirectional: one edge peers both ways.

edge_joins.description: Range host to domain. The host is joined to the domain the edge points at. Logical membership, drawn as a badge rather than nesting, because a host is physically in a subnet and logically in a domain at once.

edge_trusts.description: Domain to domain. Carries the trust direction, type, and transitivity. A two way trust is one edge with direction bidirectional, which the compiler expands to both sides.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: bidirectional (default): a two-way trust. inbound and outbound both build a one-way trust in which the source domain trusts the target.

trust_type.title: Trust type
trust_type.description: parent_child: the target is a child domain of the source. forest: a trust between two forests. external and tree_root are not built yet. Empty picks parent_child when one name ends with the other, else forest.

transitive.title: Transitive
transitive.description: Shown in the briefing. Parent and child and forest trusts are transitive in Windows either way.
